newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen flat or slightly down.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen flat or slightly down.

text.p: Polish shares on Monday eased from a 33-month high and analysts said the market would likely stabilise or fall in profit-taking following its recent surge fuelled by apparent foreign buying.
"The press has been talking about the inflow of money from investment funds, which should protect against any significant fall," said Cezary Markiewicz of Bank Gdanski brokerage.

Analysts said the main market, currently just below 16,000 points, could find support at around 15,500 or 15,000 points before proving strong enough to rally before hitting a more significant correction.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.2 percent to 15,944.9 points and turnover eased 4.4 percent to 172.8 million zlotys ($58.4 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 44 to 20 with 22 stocks flat.
Analysts said investors would be watching the release of the remainder of firms' December earnings reports, with roughly half of companies publishing figures after Monday's session.
They said the 9.5-percent rise by Monday's top gainer, drug maker Jelfa, was spurred by good December earnings.

Analysts said garment makers Bytom and Vistula, which fell 9.9 percent and 5.9 percent respectively, were hurt by news they were cutting or mulling cutting jobs to correspond to lower production plans.

Mass privatisation NFI units rose 3.3 percent to 157.5 ($53.3) zlotys in 38.7-million-zloty ($13.1 million) trade and fell 0.6 percent to 155.5 zlotys ($52.6) in 16.2-million-zloty ($5.5 million) continous trade.
Live trade turnover was at 7.1 million zlotys ($2.4 million), where seven stocks fell, five rose and six were flat.
